question: Can Illumina schematics anchor a manageable assay architecture graph, with targeted primary-source enrichment for distinctions and interfaces?
assessment_scope: Inspection of cached Illumina inventory and scraper, current DNA/RNA poster text, supplied diagram images, selected primary-paper passages, graph code and representation standards. Not a complete audit of every diagram or a new model extraction run.
observations: The original scrape saved diagram URLs but did not extract their graphical content.
The cached inventory has 154 source cards, 153 substantive/image-bearing cards and 152 unique PNG URLs. Source cards are not one-to-one with atlas technology entities.
Both inspected DNA/RNA posters state Current as of 10 November 2016. Current hosting/search dates are not scientific coverage dates.
Some poster rows combine methods, including ChIP-seq/ChIP-exo/HT-ChIP/Mint-ChIP. A shown operation cannot automatically be assigned to every named method.
Illumina's selected reference may be a later protocol or application rather than the original method publication.
A modified RASL assay retains broad anneal/ligate/amplify stages but changes the ligase and acceptor-probe terminal chemistry. Broad stage labels alone can hide a consequential distinction.

proposed_contract.target: An evidence-supported assay architecture that preserves the measurement logic, consequential interfaces and supported differences from named baselines.
proposed_contract.starting_sources: Illumina method schematic and description; larger methods-collection schematic or original-paper schematic when needed. Register method/variant scope and diagram region.
retain_for_each_transformation: Input material and relevant molecular/physical features
Action or mechanism, with catalyst/enabling reagent when consequential
Information introduced, retained, lost or selected
Order, branches and relevant input/output interfaces
expand_from_primary_sources_when: A grouped schematic does not resolve which steps apply to the method variant
The claimed difference is hidden inside a broad stage
Substrate ends, attachment, compartment or information association are needed to understand a transformation
The next stage's relevant requirements cannot be assessed
The biological interpretation or selectivity would otherwise be misleading
Historical development or comparative performance is asserted
proposed_contract.detail_relevance_rule: Retain a detail when omitting it changes target/selectivity, encoding, a consequential interface or the supported distinction being recorded. This rule is a proposed engineering criterion requiring evaluation.
proposed_contract.omission_policy: Distinguish detail outside architecture scope from unresolved architecture-critical evidence. Never promote missing evidence to a claim of biological impossibility.
proposed_contract.stopping_rule: All in-scope diagram transformations and branches are accounted for; the supported assay distinction and relevant interfaces are explicit; unresolved consequential claims remain flagged. Full executable protocol completeness is a different target.

chemical_representation.adopt_principle: Rhea reactive-part representation for macromolecules; BioPAX molecular identity plus relevant features; SBGN separation of entities, processes and catalysts.
chemical_representation.optional_identifiers: Established chemical identifiers or structure strings for known molecules/local reactive structures. Do not require a complete atom-level representation of arbitrary polymers or specimens.
chemical_representation.limitation: A molecular formula does not specify connectivity, sequence, compartment, bead attachment or barcode correspondence. Structure matching and reaction balancing do not establish assay compatibility.
chemical_representation.example: ClickSeq: 3-prime azido cDNA and a 5-prime alkyne-modified adapter undergo copper-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloaddition to produce a triazole-linked product, with downstream amplification supported in the reported workflow.

connection_policy.historical: Use verified method/version dates and cited methodological relationships to retrieve candidate predecessors. Require evidence for directed development; chronology and similarity alone are insufficient.
connection_policy.shared_transformations: Compare input/transformation/output and relevant information/context features. Preserve purpose similarity separately from shared mechanism. Neither implies interchangeability or descent.
connection_policy.comparison: Record shared features, specific changes and their supported consequences against a named baseline. A pairwise difference is not proof of global novelty.
connection_policy.scaling: Chronological processing avoids duplicate directions but leaves 20,100 unique method pairs for 201 methods. Use citation and contextual retrieval before expensive alignment.
connection_policy.alignment: Allow one-to-many connected-operation correspondences. Use graph algorithms to check topology and summarize reviewed correspondences, not to infer biochemical equivalence from labels.
connection_policy.representation: Retain multiple relationship types and multiple parents. A tree can be a display projection; the underlying scientific representation remains a graph.

minimal_harness_change: Add a diagram-and-caption source path with region-based provenance and preserved originals.
Change extraction completion criteria to architecture scope with explicit expansion triggers.
Reuse the current State/Operation/Flow representation, source tools, independent review and graph assembly.
Give the extractor diagram context plus primary papers; have a fresh reviewer check omitted distinctions, unsupported expansions and variant leakage.
Use detailed existing extractions as linked refinements rather than silently replacing or claiming a new evaluation of them.
Keep matching as a separate reviewed stage. Do not add specialist agents until a measured failure motivates them.

cases: ClickSeq: clear diagram-level architecture with consequential chemical interface
cP-RNA-seq: terminal-state-dependent selection and specificity qualifications
ChIP-seq and ChIP-exo: grouped-diagram trap and added exonuclease distinction
Original and Rnl2-based RASL: similar stage names hiding probe/ligase changes
proposed_pilot.comparison: Existing paper-first extraction versus diagram-first extraction with targeted enrichment; same model and available sources. Independently annotate necessary facts and distinctions before running.
measures: Shared-mechanism precision and false historical connections
Number of records, additional source reads and elapsed time
proposed_pilot.interpretation: A smaller graph is useful only if it preserves required distinctions and evidence. Faster extraction alone does not validate the representation or establish improved invention performance.
